tonight.headline: Josh Allen is the only starter either side has in tonight's game.
body: Nothing has kicked off. ESPN's live projection has this at 126.2 to 125.1 — a one-point game, and the win probability is an even 50. Buffalo host Detroit at 18:15 Mexico City, about two hours from now, and Josh Allen at 22.9 is the only starting player in that game on either roster.

Panda Attack moved Dalton Kincaid out of their tight end slot at 16:01 UTC today and started Harold Fannin Jr. instead, which takes their only other Buffalo–Detroit piece off the board tonight. So tonight is a free roll: whatever Allen scores is a lead you carry into Sunday against nobody. There is nothing to do before kickoff — your lineup is already the one this brief would write.

case.label: The script that beats you
case.body: Panda Attack start three running backs — Chase Brown, Saquon Barkley and Javonte Williams in the RB/WR flex — for 50.0 projected. Your two backs project 28.6. If that gap holds you need Jefferson, Garrett Wilson and McLaurin to beat their 43.3 from Pickens, Adams and Fannin, and you need Allen tonight to have already banked the difference.

case.label: Where the game actually turns
case.body: Davante Adams and Harrison Mevis both play Monday night at the Rams, and so does your Isaiah Likely. Roughly 34 of their points and 11.6 of yours resolve after everyone else has finished. A one-point projection means this game is decided on Monday night, not Sunday.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Panda Attack carry Jalen Hurts at 20.1 on their bench behind Dak Prescott at 20.3. If they start Hurts over Prescott, or swap Waddle in for Adams, their Sunday number moves and the Monday leverage shrinks. Nothing you do tonight affects either.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Pitts's game starts Sun 11:00 Mexico City
doFirst.title: Drop Kyle Pitts, add Mack Hollins
doFirst.subtitle: Carried from this morning unchanged, and the one piece of reporting that could have killed it came back the other way. Still not executed — Pitts is still on your bench.

case.label: The drop, which is the whole card
case.body: Chem's flex is slot 3, RB/WR only. Isaiah Likely holds the single tight end slot on an intact thesis — 8 targets, 8 catches, 78 yards and two touchdowns in his Giants debut. Kyle Pitts cannot enter your lineup in any week Likely is available, so his 11.3 projection is unreachable and his effective projection is zero. STRATEGY.md section 9 says it in one line: a second startable tight end has real value in IPADE and none in Chem, do not carry one.

case.label: Why he is not even insurance
case.body: New this run: Likely plays Monday night at the Rams, 18:15 Mexico City. Pitts plays Sunday at 11:00. If Likely is ruled out on Monday afternoon, Pitts will already have played twenty-five hours earlier. He cannot cover the one risk people keep him for. The actual insurance for Likely is Mark Andrews, who is free on this wire — see the watch list.

case.label: The add, and who it is contested with
case.body: A.J. Brown is on injured reserve for New England and will miss six games. Yahoo's positional column, published this week, names Mack Hollins as the man who leads New England in receiving while he is out: Hollins already holds the outside role, took 18 of the first 32 snaps — the most of any Patriots receiver besides Brown — and went 4 for 51 in Week 1 at a 13.3-yard average depth of target.

case.label: Where I am on thin ice
case.body: The market disagrees with me and says so loudly. Romeo Doubs is 60.6% rostered nationally and free on this wire, against Hollins at 5.8%, and ESPN projects Doubs 10.6 to Hollins 8.4. Doubs also played 40 snaps in Week 1 to Hollins's partial count. My reason for staying with Hollins is narrow and I want it on the record: the thesis written yesterday said it would be falsified if beat reporting named Douglas or Doubs rather than Hollins, the one column that addresses the question directly named Hollins, and overriding a tested thesis on an ownership percentage is the churn STRATEGY.md section 3 exists to stop. If you would rather own the more valuable player than the better-reported one, take Doubs — the drop is the same either way and that is the part that matters.

case.label: The third name nobody is picking
case.body: DeMario Douglas drew a team-high 7 targets in Week 1 and caught 5 of them for 20 yards. In full PPR, seven targets is the currency and twenty yards is not the story. He is 2.3% rostered. If the first New England box score after this reads Douglas 8 targets, both Hollins and Doubs were wrong and this seat changes hands again.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Likely appears on a Giants injury report before Monday, which makes Pitts the only tight end you own and reverses this the same hour. Or Hollins takes under four targets at Pittsburgh while Doubs or Douglas clears seven. Or Chem changes slot 3 to RB/WR/TE, which makes Pitts startable and kills the structural half outright.

action.label: Add Mack Hollins · drop Kyle Pitts

whatWentWrong.title: This card is twenty-six hours old and Pitts is still on your roster
whatWentWrong.lead: It was written at 13:00 yesterday as DEPTH, upgraded to SOLID at 13:00 today, and has not been executed. The window is not indefinite: Atlanta kick off Sunday at 11:00 Mexico City and a player whose game has started cannot be dropped.

case.label: What it has cost so far
case.body: Nothing yet, because Pitts has not played since the card was written. That is luck rather than judgement. The cost arrives at 11:00 Sunday, when Pitts locks into a bench seat for the week and the seat cannot be used for anyone.

case.label: Why it keeps not happening
case.body: The card asks you to drop a 93.7%-rostered tight end for a 5.8%-rostered receiver, which reads wrong at a glance and is right on the structure. That is a presentation problem in the card, not an error in it, and it is worth naming rather than restating the same card a fourth time.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: If you are not going to make this move, say so by keeping Pitts through Sunday and the thesis closes CHURN on Tuesday rather than staying open and being rewritten every twelve hours. Either outcome is better than a card that lives forever.

whatWentWrong.sources: Chem decision log · ESPN league data

whatWentWrong.title: Jalen Coker was limited again on Thursday, and that is why there is only one seat to work with
whatWentWrong.lead: Second consecutive limited practice with the ankle. He was claimed at 07:14 on Wednesday, so the churn rule closes his seat until 22 September regardless of what the designation says.

case.label: The practice trend
case.body: Yahoo's Thursday report has Coker limited for the second straight day, and notes he was in a walking boot on Monday. Boot to limited to limited is trending up, not down. Dave Canales has expressed 'little, if any doubt' about Sunday.

case.label: Why it constrains the rest of the brief
case.body: Your bench is Tuten, Pitts, Monangai, Brian Thomas Jr. and Coker. Three of those five carry questionable tags, Coker's seat is closed by the seven-day churn window and Tuten is your only healthy flex fallback. That leaves exactly one seat — Pitts's — available for any add this week, which is why Woody Marks and Mark Andrews are on the watch list rather than in a card.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Coker carries OUT or DOUBTFUL into Sunday, which kills the seat outright and reopens it on Tuesday 22 September. Full participation Friday with no designation reinstates the original claim thesis and makes him a flex candidate over Tuten.

worthALook.name: Mark Andrews
worthALook.lead: Zay Flowers did not practise Wednesday with a hamstring, and the best tight end on any wire in either league just got a target projection to match.

case.label: What changed today
case.body: Baltimore's report has Zay Flowers as a did-not-participate with a hamstring. SI's Week 2 must-start column now projects Andrews for double-digit targets against New Orleans, on the reasoning that with Flowers out the passing game runs through Andrews and then through Rashod Bateman, Chris Moore and LaJohntay Wester. He went 4 for 49 on 6 targets in Week 1 without that vacancy.

case.label: Why he is still not a card
case.body: The same structure that makes Pitts worthless makes Andrews worthless. Chem's flex is RB/WR. Andrews would sit behind Likely in the only tight end slot you have, and adding him means carrying a second tight end — the exact thing STRATEGY.md section 9 tells you not to do in this league. He is the best player available on this wire and he does not fit the roster, and those two facts are both true.

case.label: The honest counter
case.body: Likely projects 11.6 and Andrews 10.3, which is close enough that if the Giants plan changes — Nabers back to full health, Theo Johnson taking the 11-personnel snaps — Andrews becomes the better starter outright rather than insurance. That is a week-4 question on the current evidence, not a week-2 one.

case.label: When to act
case.body: The hour Isaiah Likely appears on a Giants injury report. He plays Monday night, so New York's Friday and Saturday reports are the trigger, and Andrews is free until someone else takes him. Also act if Likely draws under four targets at the Rams, which would be the first real crack in a thesis that has only strengthened so far.

worthALook.name: Romeo Doubs
worthALook.lead: The other side of the A.J. Brown vacancy, rostered by three in five leagues nationally and free in this one.

case.label: The anomaly
case.body: 60.6% rostered nationally, free here, ownership up 0.86 on the day. STRATEGY.md section 4 ranks ownership anomaly third among all add signals and above ownership velocity, and this is the second-largest one on the Chem board behind Mark Andrews.

case.label: The reason he is not the named add
case.body: 40 snaps in Week 1 and zero catches. He dropped a pass and was the downfield target on Drake Maye's first interception. Yahoo's column on who inherits A.J. Brown's work picks Hollins ahead of him on the grounds that Hollins already holds the outside role. The projection disagrees — ESPN has Doubs 10.6 to Hollins 8.4 — and I have taken the reporting over the projection, which is the call in this brief most likely to be wrong.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Doubs clearing six targets at Pittsburgh, or a New England beat report naming him as the primary outside receiver. Either makes him the right man for the Pitts seat and the Hollins card becomes a Doubs card at the same price.

worthALook.name: Woody Marks
worthALook.lead: The only player on waivers in this league, clearing at 01:00 Friday Mexico City — and the reporting on him does not support spending a seat.

case.label: The clock
case.body: Marks is the single WAIVERS-status player on the Chem board and he clears at 07:00 UTC tonight, which is 01:00 Friday in Mexico City. This 16:00 brief is the last one before that. In Chem priority resets weekly so a claim is genuinely free, but AVIATO sit 10th of 10 in the order this week, so a claim would most likely lose to any of the nine teams above you. Nicky Jam dropped him at 03:37 this morning to add KC Concepcion — a manager looked at him and moved on, which is information, not proof.

case.label: The reporting is split and neither half is current
case.body: One Yahoo piece has Marks passing Nick Chubb on the Houston depth chart during Joe Mixon's absence. A CBS note says he is 'unlikely to see his workload increase' — but that note describes an 0-2 Houston team facing Jacksonville, so it is a different week and I am not going to pretend it applies. I could not retrieve a dated Week 2 Houston usage report.

case.label: The seat problem
case.body: Even if the claim were free and the reporting were good, there is no seat. Your five bench places are Tuten, Pitts, Monangai, Thomas and Coker; Pitts's is spoken for by the Hollins card and Coker's is closed by the churn rule until 22 September. A claim would have to drop a questionable player before his designation is known, which is how you lose a Monangai.

case.label: When to act
case.body: If Houston name Marks the lead back on the Friday or Saturday report, he becomes worth a free claim next Tuesday rather than tonight, by which point he will be a free agent here anyway. Or if Warren or Achane appears on a Friday injury report, which turns a speculative claim into one for a real hole.

doNotChase.name: 49ers D/ST
doNotChase.lead: The largest single-day ownership move anywhere on the Chem board for the second run running, and the required weekly comparison still comes back hold.

case.label: The comparison, which is the point of this row
case.body: San Francisco are 6th of 32 on Pro Football Network's Week 2 defence board and Baltimore are 9th. ESPN project San Francisco 7.8 and Baltimore 7.6. That is three places and two tenths of a point.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Two tenths. STRATEGY.md forbids proposing a move worth under a point, and this seat has already changed hands three times in eight days with two CHURN entries in the decision log. San Francisco is genuinely the better draw — they held the Rams to seven points, they are off extra rest from a Thursday game and Miami were poor in Week 1 — and none of that is worth two tenths.

case.label: Where the boards disagree
case.body: Yesterday's brief used FantasyPros, which had Baltimore 3rd and San Francisco 4th. PFN today has Baltimore 9th and San Francisco 6th. Both boards put San Francisco ahead; they disagree on how far. I am reporting the wider of the two gaps rather than the one that flatters the hold.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Baltimore finishing outside the top 12 defensive scores in Week 2 while San Francisco finish top 5. Then the churn rule cost real points, the seat opens on Tuesday and San Francisco is first on the list.

doNotChase.name: Carson Wentz
doNotChase.lead: The loudest story on this wire, worth reading and worth nothing to you.

case.label: The story
case.body: Kyler Murray is in concussion protocol after a first-quarter hit in Week 1. ESPN's Dan Graziano has Murray starting if he clears in time and Wentz starting if he does not, with J.J. McCarthy third. Minnesota are taking it day by day. ESPN project Wentz at 17.1 this week, which is a real number.

case.label: The number that kills the case
case.body: His season projection on this wire is 0.5. Whatever ESPN think of his Sunday, they do not think he holds the job. You start Josh Allen, who projects 22.9 tonight and 385.3 for the season and is the consensus QB1 overall. There is no version of this roster where a Minnesota backup is startable.

case.label: Where he does matter
case.body: Not as an add — as the reason Justin Jefferson's tile is green. Wentz entered in Week 1 and Jefferson went 8 catches on 9 targets for 92 yards and two touchdowns; Jefferson's own line was that Wentz 'knew the entire game plan and executed it without missing a beat'. The quarterback change is a reason to start Jefferson confidently, not a reason to buy the quarterback.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nothing that does not also involve Josh Allen getting hurt. If that happens this is a live conversation and Bo Nix at 84.3% rostered, also free here, is ahead of Wentz in it.

doNotChase.name: Jordan Addison
doNotChase.lead: 75% rostered, free here, and declined for the third consecutive run so that a future brief does not rediscover him as a find.

case.label: The anomaly is real
case.body: JuiceJam dropped him at 07:14 on Wednesday to claim Devaughn Vele. A 75.2%-rostered receiver sitting free in a ten-team league is exactly the `why=OWNED` signal STRATEGY.md section 4 ranks third, and it is the reason this row keeps needing to be written.

case.label: The number that kills the case
case.body: Target order. T.J. Hockenson — a tight end — is Minnesota's second target behind Jefferson at 81% route share and 16% target share, which puts Addison third at best. Ownership moved -0.36 today, so the market is still walking away rather than not noticing.

case.label: And the seat
case.body: Same constraint as everywhere else in this brief: one open seat, spoken for. Adding Addison would mean dropping a questionable player before Friday's designations, which is the specific mistake the Monangai entry in the decision log exists to prevent.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Murray clearing protocol and Addison drawing seven or more targets at Chicago, or Jefferson missing time. Either makes him the second read rather than the third, and at 75% rostered he will not still be free by then.

settled.title: Hold Isaiah Likely over Kyle Pitts at tight end (14 September)
settled.result: Holding. Likely went 8 of 8 for 78 and two scores in his Giants debut and nothing this week touches it. The corollary — that Pitts is therefore dead weight in this league — is the card at the top of this brief.

settled.title: Start McLaurin in the RB/WR flex over Tuten (15 September)
settled.result: Holding. McLaurin is not on Washington's Week 2 injury report and the quad clause is clean. Dallas allowed the 13th-most fantasy points per target to perimeter receivers in Week 1. Tuten's own matchup got worse: FTN say sit him at Denver.

settled.title: Claim Tyler Loop, drop Chris Boswell (16 September)
settled.result: Holding, fourth consecutive run. PFN have Loop K4. Best actually available on this wire is Eddy Pineiro at K4 on the same board — and he is QUESTIONABLE, which is the reason not to chase the higher projection. Then Cairo Santos K7 at 8.6, identical to Loop. Nothing beats him.

settled.title: Hold the Ravens defence rather than churn to San Francisco (16 September)
settled.result: Holding, but the gap widened. PFN have Baltimore 9th and San Francisco 6th today where FantasyPros had them 3rd and 4th yesterday. Two tenths of an ESPN point either way, which is under the bar.

settled.title: Hold Kyle Monangai rather than drop him (16 September)
settled.result: Holding. Limited Wednesday and Thursday with the knee, and D'Andre Swift was limited Thursday too. Neither falsification condition — Swift taking the receiving role back, or Monangai under 40% of snaps — can resolve until Sunday.

settled.title: Hold Brian Thomas Jr. through the shoulder scare (12 September, reviewed four times)
settled.result: Holding. Limited with the shoulder again this week, Liam Coen 'fully imagines him being able to play', and Jakobi Meyers is limited alongside him with a thumb injury — which weakens the 'Meyers out-targets him' clause rather than settling it. The production half of the thesis is still unproven at 3 catches for 40.

settled.title: Claim Jalen Coker, drop Matthew Stafford (14–16 September)
settled.result: The claim landed and the player has not. Limited Wednesday and limited again Thursday with the ankle. He has been on the roster two days, has not been startable for either of them, and the churn rule now closes his seat until 22 September. The claim was defensible; it has cost you a bench seat in the week you needed one.

settled.title: Downgrade the Pitts/Hollins card to DEPTH (17 September, 04:05)
settled.result: Still a miss, and now a compounding one. It was restored to SOLID at 13:00 and it is 16:05 and Pitts is still rostered. A card that changes tier twice in a day is a card nobody acts on.

settled.title: McLaurin + Stafford for DeVonta Smith (14–15 September)
settled.result: Dead and staying dead. The Coker claim dropped Stafford at 07:14 and took the offer with it. Not acted on, no harm done, and it does not come back — the exhaustive pair search below found no Chem trade at all.

cannotSee.label: Friday's designations, which decide three of your five bench players
cannotSee.body: Coker (ankle), Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) and Monangai (knee) all carry questionable tags off Thursday practice. Thursday is the second of three reports; Friday is the one that produces the game designation. This brief is written before it exists. Re-check all three before 11:00 Sunday.

cannotSee.label: Whether Kyler Murray clears concussion protocol
cannotSee.body: Justin Jefferson's GREAT tile assumes Carson Wentz throws. Graziano's framing on 16 September was that Murray starts if he clears in time and Wentz starts if he does not, and Minnesota were taking it day by day. I found no Thursday update either way. The tile survives both outcomes — Jefferson is a top-six receiver against a secondary that allowed 353 yards and three touchdowns in Week 1 — but the margin is smaller if Murray plays cold.

cannotSee.label: Who is throwing to Garrett Wilson, corroborated but not confirmed
cannotSee.body: The runbook's own worst case is a pass-catcher started behind a quarterback nobody looked up, so this is worth being precise about. I could not retrieve a beat report naming the Jets' Week 2 starter — two searches and the ESPN depth chart, which returned blank. Two independent routes give the same answer: Geno Smith at 15.4 projected is the only quarterback New York have anywhere in this data set, and this morning's run reached the same name from its own research. Every other quarterback in this brief — Willis for Achane, Rodgers for Warren, Daniels for McLaurin, Dart for Likely, Young for Coker, Lawrence for Tuten and Thomas, Penix questionable for Pitts — is carried from that run rather than re-verified this afternoon. The only one re-checked today is Minnesota's, because it decides Jefferson's tile.

cannotSee.label: Ten of your fourteen matchup tiles are not researched
cannotSee.body: I graded four this run: Chicago against the pass for Jefferson, Dallas against perimeter receivers for McLaurin, San Francisco as a unit for Achane, and Baltimore for the defence. Detroit, New England, Green Bay, the Rams, Denver, Atlanta and Minnesota are dashed because I did not look them up, not because they are average. Achane's SHAKY is a team-defence read, not a rank against running backs specifically, and it is the weakest of the four.

cannotSee.label: Season projections are frozen and every trade priced on them is suspect
cannotSee.body: Bhayshul Tuten's seasonProj has read 205.2 on the 15, 16 and 17 September snapshots while his weekly projection moved 9.4 to 10.1 to 10.1. The IPADE trade arithmetic produces exactly the same +40.6 across all three. The weekly number is live; the season number appears to be a preseason artifact. That is why this brief contains no Chem trade even though the pair search is priced on it.

cannotSee.label: No Chem trade exists, and here is exactly what I tested
cannotSee.body: Every one-for-one pairing between your fourteen players and all 126 players on the other nine rosters, scored on both sides' optimal lineups: zero produced a gain for both teams. Two-for-one consolidation produced two, both nonsense — Tuten plus Loop to Nicky Jam for Cameron Dicker, which trades a flex body for a kicker, and McLaurin plus Pitts for Colston Loveland, which gives up your flex starter for a tight end you cannot flex. Your only genuine surplus is Pitts, and nobody in this league needs a tight end.

cannotSee.label: Rival pending waiver claims are invisible
cannotSee.body: ESPN only ever returns your own. Woody Marks clears at 01:00 Friday and any of the nine teams ahead of you in the order can have him. Mark Andrews at 82.2% and Romeo Doubs at 60.6% are free agents right now and either can be gone before you next open this.
